Fact.Name: Modified adjusted gross income for the education credits (section 25A(d)(2))
Fact.Description:
MAGI for the American Opportunity and Lifetime Learning phaseouts: AGI increased by the section 911, 931 and 933 exclusions.
ONE NAMED FACT for the four sites (two per credit, an IsComplete guard and a value read) that need MAGI rather than AGI.
THE STATUTE IS EXPLICIT AND NAMES THREE SECTIONS, not the four-item form list the other surfaces print: section 25A(d)(2) says MAGI "means adjusted gross income of the taxpayer for the taxable year increased by any amount excluded from gross income under section 911, 931, or 933". The mapping to shipping facts is one-to-one: section 933 -> ctcOdc:/puertoRicoIncomeExclusion933 section 911 -> ctcOdc:/sched8812Line2bForm2555Exclusions (Form 2555 lines 45 and 50, which together are the section 911 earned-income and housing exclusions) section 931 -> ctcOdc:/possessionIncomeExclusion931 (Form 4563 line 15) Section 24(b)(1) uses the identical formula, which is why Schedule 8812's line-2d total is the right shape to borrow — but it is borrowed as a QUANTITY, and the authority cited here is section 25A(d)(2) itself.
COMPLETENESS: all three add-backs are complete-safe, so this is Complete exactly when /agi is. ONE QUANTITY, ONE FACT: this is a direct alias of ctcOdc /modifiedAgiWithForeignAndPossessionExclusions, the single root for the AGI + sections 911/931/933 modified AGI that this and four sibling surfaces define identically; the add-back list lives on the root.

Fact.Name: Filer is claimed as a dependent on another taxpayer's return (section 25A(g)(3)(A) categorical bar)
Fact.Description:
TRUE when either filer on this return is claimed as a dependent by another taxpayer (filers:/eitherFilerIsClaimedAsDependent). Section 25A(g)(3)(A) is categorical: where a section 151 deduction with respect to an individual is ALLOWED to another taxpayer, "no credit shall be allowed under subsection (a) to such individual for such individual's taxable year" — so a filer who is actually claimed as a dependent gets NO education credit on THIS return, whichever student's expenses are entered. The bar turns on the deduction being allowed, not on the individual merely being claimABLE. This is a return-level bar, not a per-student one, because the module tracks Part III at a single return-level scope with no student identity beyond the print-only name/TIN facts. It does NOT apply to a return that claims a dependent's own expenses under section 25A(g)(3)(B): that student is the taxpayer's dependent, not a filer on this return, and the read is scoped to the two filers for exactly that reason.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE ON AN UNANSWERED dependency attestation: an unanswered question leaves this return's education credit standing rather than zeroing it, the same direction the shipped filers:/filers/*/hsaDeductionDeniedAsDependent readers use. This is a disclosed, deliberate choice: defaulting the credit to $0 on every return before that single checkbox is answered would be a large regression for a condition that is FALSE for the overwhelming majority of filers, the same precedent as the Part III eligibility gate (favourable answers restore the value; the flow must ask).

Fact.Name: Adjusted qualified education expenses for the American Opportunity Credit (Form 8863 line 27)
Fact.Description: The adjusted qualified education expenses (tuition, required fees, course materials) for the single eligible student for whom the American Opportunity Credit is claimed — Form 8863 Part III line 27, "Don't enter more than $4,000". Supplied directly as a taxpayer input (net of tax-free assistance). Complete-safe: 0 / unanswered ⇒ no AOTC ⇒ /americanOpportunityCredit (line 29) and /sched3Line3 unchanged. Scope: one student; married-filing-separately filers are ineligible (credit 0); the Part III student-eligibility gates (first 4 years, ≥ half-time, no prior 4-year claim, no felony drug conviction) are applied by /aotcStudentEligibleForAotc, not by this intake.

Fact.Name: Adjusted American Opportunity qualified expenses, floored at zero
Fact.Description: The computational form of Form 8863 Part III line 27: an answered qualified-expense amount cannot contribute a negative amount to the American Opportunity Credit, so it is the greater of /writableAotcQualifiedExpenses and the structural zero floor. The writable carries the form's $0 minimum, but this explicit floor keeps the credit arithmetic safe even when a persisted or test input bypasses that intake limit. Unanswered is complete-safe zero so guarded credit branches do not manufacture an incomplete result.

Fact.Name: A prior American Opportunity Credit claim was finally determined to be due to fraud or to reckless or intentional disregard of the rules
Fact.Description:
The IRC 25A(b)(4)(A) intake: whether there has been a final determination, for any earlier taxable year, that the taxpayer's claim of the American Opportunity Tax Credit was due to fraud, or was due to reckless or intentional disregard of rules and regulations. The Instructions for Form 8863 print the rule as a Caution directly under the American Opportunity Credit heading, so it is a printed condition of allowance and not an inference.
A WRITABLE AND NOT A DERIVATION, for the same reason ctcOdc:/receivedImproperClaims is one: the return carries nothing about an earlier year's examination, and a final determination is a Service action this dictionary has no other record of.
THIS IS A DIFFERENT RULE FROM /aotc8862Required, which models IRC 25A(b)(4)(B): that one is a recertification a denied taxpayer can satisfy by filing Form 8862, and it lifts as soon as the information the Secretary requires is supplied. IRC 25A(b)(4)(A) is an absolute time bar that no form lifts; only the running of the period lifts it. A return can be subject to either, both, or neither.
SCOPE, stated rather than left to be discovered: the statute bars only the American Opportunity Tax Credit. The Lifetime Learning Credit is not barred by this subparagraph, and because /llcAotcSameStudentCoordinationMet reads /aotcTentativeCredit, a barred return's Part II line 10 expenses are freed to the Lifetime Learning Credit exactly as a Part III Stop answer frees them.

Fact.Name: The IRC 25A(b)(4)(A) disallowance period has run
Fact.Description:
The second IRC 25A(b)(4)(A) intake: whether the disallowance period that began with that final determination has already run, so that 2025 is no longer a taxable year inside it. The period is 10 taxable years after the most recent taxable year for which the determination was fraud, and 2 taxable years after the most recent taxable year for which it was reckless or intentional disregard.
ASKED AND NOT DERIVED, the same choice ctcOdc:/improperClaimsNoticeExpired records for IRC 24(g): the period runs from the most recent taxable year for which there was a final determination, a year this return does not capture anywhere. Deriving it would need a prior-year intake this dictionary does not have.
THE QUESTION IS MANDATORY ONCE /writableAotcPriorFraudOrRecklessDisregardDetermination IS TRUE, and /aotcBarredByDisallowancePeriod is built so that leaving it unanswered BARS the credit rather than allowing it. That is the same posture the Form 8862 Part IV pair already takes inside /aotcStudentEligibleForAotc: once the recertification is required, an unanswered line 19a bars. The interview must therefore ask this question whenever the first one is answered yes; a return that never reaches the first question is unaffected, because the bar is complete-safe false without it.

Fact.Name: IRC 25A(b)(4)(A): this return sits inside an American Opportunity Credit disallowance period
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the taxpayer has answered that a prior American Opportunity Credit claim was finally determined to be due to fraud or to reckless or intentional disregard of the rules, AND has not answered that the resulting disallowance period has run. The statute allows NO American Opportunity Tax Credit for any taxable year in that period, so this fact is consumed as a bar inside /aotcStudentEligibleForAotc.
COMPLETE SAFE FALSE, deliberately: the first limb is All(IsComplete(intake), intake), so a return that was never asked the question resolves this fact Complete false and its American Opportunity Credit is exactly what it was before this fact existed. No existing return moves.
THE UNANSWERED EXPIRY ARM BARS, and that asymmetry is the point. Once the determination is answered yes, Not(All(IsComplete(hasRun), hasRun)) is TRUE while the expiry question is unanswered, so the credit is barred until the taxpayer says the period has run. An unanswered expiry may not be read as an expired period: the statute's default after a final determination is that the bar applies, and the taxpayer is the only party who knows the determination year. The Form 8862 Part IV pair inside /aotcStudentEligibleForAotc takes the same posture once /aotc8862Required is true.
WHY THIS IS NOT A REFUSAL. A knockout would stop the return; this only zeroes one credit, which is what the statute does. The filer keeps the Lifetime Learning Credit, and /llcAotcSameStudentCoordinationMet frees the Part II line 10 expenses because /aotcTentativeCredit is no longer above zero.
WHAT IS NOT MODELLED, named rather than left to be discovered: the determination YEAR, and therefore the arithmetic of the 10-year and 2-year periods, is not in this dictionary. This fact relies on the taxpayer's own answer about whether the period has run. A prior-year intake carrying the most recent determination year is what a derivation would need.

Fact.Name: The American Opportunity Credit is allowed for this student: Form 8863 Part III lines 23 through 26, Form 8862 Part IV lines 19a/19b when the recertification is required, and the IRC 25A(b)(4)(A) disallowance period
Fact.Description:
The American Opportunity Credit eligibility gate. /aotcTentativeCredit reads it, so every printed "Stop!" answer on Part III stops the credit: a filer who answers line 23 Yes ("the American opportunity credit HAS been claimed for this student for 4 prior tax years"), or line 24 No, or line 25 Yes, or line 26 Yes receives no credit, and the Form 8862 Part IV recertification pair is read the same way.
FOUR PART III LIMBS, AND THE POLARITY IS NOT UNIFORM. Three of the four bar on Yes and one bars on No, exactly as printed: line 23 "Has the American opportunity credit been claimed for this student for any 4 prior tax years?" Yes stops, so the limb is answered AND false; line 24 "Was the student enrolled at least half-time ...?" NO stops, so the limb is answered AND true, the only affirmative limb here; line 25 "Did the student complete the first 4 years of postsecondary education before 2025?" Yes stops, so answered AND false; line 26 "Was the student convicted, before the end of 2025, of a felony for possession or distribution of a controlled substance?" Yes stops, so answered AND false.
COMPLETE SAFE IN THE /form5695SectionAQualified SHAPE, IsComplete(x) AND "x or Not(x)" per limb, so an unanswered question resolves this fact FALSE rather than leaving it unresolved. That is what keeps /aotcTentativeCredit, /aotcCreditAfterPhaseout and every education credit total Complete on a return that never reached Part III. IT IS ALSO A VALUE CHANGE: a return that claims AOTC expenses without answering lines 23 through 26 computes a $0 credit, where an unguarded read would compute up to $2,500. The four answers are favourable on any real Part III return, so adding them restores the old value exactly; the flow must ask them.
THE FORM 8862 LIMB IS CONDITIONAL, AND ITS OWN POLARITY TRAP IS AVOIDED DELIBERATELY. /aotc8862Required is a bare writable Boolean with no complete safe wrapper, so writing it as another All(IsComplete(req), req, ...) limb would resolve FALSE on every return that never answered the recertification question and would bar the credit for everyone. The limb is instead Any(Not(answered AND required), the 19a/19b test): a return that is not required to recertify passes the limb on the first arm, and only a return that answers /aotc8862Required true has to satisfy Form 8862 line 19a Yes AND line 19b No, which is the Caution printed under those two boxes.
THE TWO "4 PRIOR YEARS" INTAKES ARE READ SEPARATELY, NOT MERGED. The audit row asked for /writableAotcClaimedForFourPriorTaxYears (Form 8862 line 19b) to be merged into /writableAotcStudentClaimedForFourPriorTaxYears (Form 8863 line 23) first. That merge is REFUSED here, on the reasons /writableAotcStudentClaimedForFourPriorTaxYears already records in its own Description: the two questions have different year anchors (line 19b counts the 4 prior years against the year entered on Form 8862 line 1, the year being recertified, which need not be 2025; line 23 counts them against this return's tax year), and the Form 8862 side is mid reshape into a per student /form8862AotcStudents collection. This gate therefore reads both intakes, and an inconsistent pair (line 23 No but line 19b Yes) bars the credit, which is the conservative and coherent reading without the merge.
obligation: closes the "PRINT ONLY until /aotcTentativeCredit consumes it" debt recorded in /writableAotcStudentClaimedForFourPriorTaxYears, /writableAotcStudentEnrolledAtLeastHalfTime, /writableAotcStudentCompletedFirstFourYears and /writableAotcStudentFelonyDrugConviction, and gives /writableAotcStudentIsEligibleStudent and /writableAotcClaimedForFourPriorTaxYears their first consumer OUTSIDE their own printed Yes/No boxes (the /pdf8862Line19a and /pdf8862Line19b Not facts already read them, which is a render concern, not a tax one).
THE IRC 25A(b)(4)(A) LIMB is why this fact is now named for ALLOWANCE and not only for the Part III questions. /aotcBarredByDisallowancePeriod is a taxpayer-level absolute bar - no American Opportunity Tax Credit for any taxable year in the disallowance period that follows a final determination of fraud or of reckless or intentional disregard - and it belongs HERE rather than on /aotcTentativeCredit because this fact is what the rest of the dictionary reads to mean that the American Opportunity Credit is allowed for this student. form8815 reads it as the IRC 135(d)(2)(A) gate on expenses taken into account in determining the credit ALLOWED, and a barred student's Part III line 27 entry is used in figuring nothing, so it must not reduce the series EE and I savings bond exclusion either. The limb is complete safe false, so no return that never answers the two new intakes moves.

Fact.Name: Nothing bars the American Opportunity Credit for this filer and this student (Form 8863 Part III lines 23-26, the IRC 25A(g)(6) MFS bar, the IRC 25A(g)(3)(A) dependent bar, and the IRC 25A(g)(1)/(g)(8) identification and payee-statement conditions)
Fact.Description:
TRUE when none of the four American Opportunity Credit bars applies: the return's filing status is not married filing separately (IRC 25A(g)(6) allows the credit on a married taxpayer's return only when a joint return is filed); the student passes the Form 8863 Part III lines 23 through 26 eligibility gate and, where required, the Form 8862 Part IV recertification and the IRC 25A(b)(4)(A) disallowance-period bar (/aotcStudentEligibleForAotc); the filer is not claimed as a dependent on another return (IRC 25A(g)(3)(A), /educationCreditFilerCanBeClaimedAsDependent); and the student's identification and payee-statement conditions of allowance are met (IRC 25A(g)(1)/(g)(8), /aotcIdentificationAndPayeeStatementMet).
ONE GATE, TWO CONSUMERS: /aotcTentativeCredit (Form 8863 Part I line 1) and /aotcPerStudentTentativeCredit (Form 8863 Part III line 30) both read this fact so a filer or student barred from the credit prints $0 at both lines rather than a credit at one and $0 at the other. The two facts still legitimately diverge on the one axis this gate does not decide: whether Part III line 27 has been answered at all. /aotcTentativeCredit is the Part I total and stays complete-safe $0 on an unanswered Part III; /aotcPerStudentTentativeCredit is the Part III worksheet cell and stays Incomplete there, matching what a filer who never claims the credit for this student leaves blank on the printed page.

Fact.Name: A taxpayer identification number on this American opportunity credit claim was issued after the return's due date
Fact.Description: Screen question, asked when American opportunity credit expenses are entered: "Was the student's taxpayer identification number, or yours (or your spouse's on a joint return), issued after the due date of your 2025 return, including extensions?" Help: the American opportunity credit is not allowed, on an original or an amended 2025 return, if the student's TIN or the taxpayer's TIN was issued after that date; the lifetime learning credit is not affected. TRUE bars the credit through /aotcBarredByTinIssuedAfterDueDate. Unanswered is read as not late: a return filed by its due date with the TIN on it could not carry a TIN issued later, so only a late or amended return can answer Yes.

Fact.Name: The American opportunity credit is barred because a TIN was issued after the due date
Fact.Description: TRUE when /writableAotcTinIssuedAfterReturnDueDate is answered Yes. Section 25A(g)(1)(B)(i) treats the student identification requirement as unmet for the American opportunity credit unless the student's TIN was issued on or before the due date of the return, and (g)(1)(B)(ii) allows no American opportunity credit when the taxpayer's TIN was issued after that date. Complete false when the question is unanswered or answered No. Read by /aotcCreditAllowedForThisFilerAndStudent, so both Part I line 1 and Part III line 30 carry $0 when it is true.

Fact.Name: An education credit is claimed for more than one student
Fact.Description: Screen question, asked when American opportunity or lifetime learning credit expenses are entered: "Are you claiming the American opportunity credit or the lifetime learning credit for more than one student?" Help: Form 8863 needs a separate Part III for each student. This return computes and prints one Part III, so a Yes refuses the return through /knockoutEducationCreditForMoreThanOneStudent rather than fold two students into one. Unanswered or No keeps the one-student return.

Fact.Name: An education credit claimed for more than one student refuses the return
Fact.Description: TRUE when /writableEducationCreditClaimedForMoreThanOneStudent is answered Yes. Form 8863 needs a Part III for each student, and the American opportunity credit is figured per student; this dictionary models one student (one set of Part III answers and one American opportunity expense entry), so a second student is refused rather than merged into the first. Complete false when the question is unanswered or answered No. Its successor is the contract constraint that names this knockout.

Fact.Name: A second institution with no Form 1098-T refuses the return
Fact.Description: TRUE when a second educational institution is named on line 22b, line 22b(2) is answered No (no 2025 Form 1098-T from it), and line 22b(3) is not answered Yes (no 2024 Form 1098-T from it with box 7 checked). Section 25A(g)(8) conditions the credit on receiving a statement furnished under section 6050S(d), and the sources vendored here do not say whether a statement from the first institution meets that condition for expenses paid to a second one, nor how the first-institution exceptions apply to it. The return is refused rather than allowed or denied on an unsettled reading. Complete false when no second institution is named, or its line 22b(2) is unanswered or Yes. Its successor is the contract constraint that names this knockout.

Fact.Name: Tentative American Opportunity Credit per student (Form 8863 lines 28-30)
Fact.Description: The per-student tentative AOTC before the MAGI phaseout: 100% of the first $2,000 of adjusted qualified expenses plus 25% of the next $2,000 (Form 8863 Part III lines 28-30), i.e. min(exp, 2000) + 25% × max(0, min(exp, 4000) − 2000); maximum $2,500. Gated on /writableAotcQualifiedExpenses being answered AND /aotcCreditAllowedForThisFilerAndStudent (the MFS bar, the Part III student-eligibility gate, the dependent bar, and the identification and payee-statement conditions). Complete-safe 0 otherwise. Rounded to whole dollars.

Fact.Name: AOTC MAGI phaseout threshold (Form 8863 line 2)
Fact.Description: Form 8863 Part I line 2: $180,000 if married filing jointly, else $90,000 (single, HoH, QSS). MFS is ineligible (handled by the credit gate). Above this MAGI the AOTC is fully phased out.

Fact.Name: AOTC MAGI phaseout range width (Form 8863 line 5)
Fact.Description: Form 8863 Part I line 5: $20,000 if married filing jointly, else $10,000. The width of the linear phaseout band below /aotcPhaseoutThreshold.

Fact.Name: AOTC after MAGI phaseout (Form 8863 Part I line 7)
Fact.Description: Form 8863 Part I line 7 = tentative AOTC × clamp((threshold − MAGI)/range, 0, 1). MAGI is /form8863Magi, adjusted gross income plus the section 911, 931 and 933 exclusions. Computed in dollar arithmetic (iraDeduction-style): line 7 = round( tentative × min(range, max(0, threshold − MAGI)) / range ). Full credit when MAGI ≤ threshold − range; 0 when MAGI ≥ threshold; linear between. Complete-safe 0 when /form8863Magi is incomplete or the tentative credit is 0. THE PHASEOUT FRACTION IS CANONICAL AT THE PRINTED LINE: line 7 reads /aotcPhaseoutFractionThousandths, the printed line 6 rounded to three decimal places and carried as integer thousandths, and divides by 1,000 only after the multiply. The form says "Multiply line 1 by line 6", so a return whose line 6 and line 7 are both printed foots exactly. One quantity, one fact: the printed ratio is the only one this module computes. This is the idiom form8839.xml /form8839Children/*/line10 already uses for its own line 6 x line 9.

Fact.Name: At least one parent alive at the end of the tax year (Form 8863 line 7, condition 2)
Fact.Description: i8863 Line 7 condition 2: "At least one of your parents was alive at the end of 2025." Asked when: a filer under 24 on a non-joint return claiming the American Opportunity Credit, OR any filer whose form8615:/form8615UnearnedIncomeOverThreshold is true (Form 8615's own condition 4 reads this same fact — the printed question is identical in both instructions). Defaults to TRUE when unanswered — see the ABSENT-ANSWER POLICY note above: TRUE makes the refundable credit LESS available, so an unanswered return under-claims rather than over-claims.

Fact.Name: Earned income did not exceed half of the filer's support (Form 8863 line 7, conditions 1b/1c)
Fact.Description:
i8863 Line 7 conditions 1(b)/1(c): "your earned income ... was less than one-half of your support". An ATTESTATION, not a computation: "support" (i8863's definition — food, shelter, clothing, medical/dental care, education, at fair market value, counting support provided by the filer, their parents AND others) is not derivable from anything in this dictionary, because support furnished by third parties is never reported on a return. Defaults to TRUE when unanswered — see the ABSENT-ANSWER POLICY note above.
BOUNDARY: the question asks the STATUTORY boundary — TRUE when the filer's earned income was NOT MORE THAN half of their own support — and no longer i8863's looser paraphrase "less than one-half". The polarity is unchanged: TRUE still means the line 7 condition is met and the refundable credit is barred; only the boundary case moves into TRUE. IRC 25A(i) hands this population to section 1(g), and section 1(g)(2)(A)(ii)(II) sets the test at earned income that "does not exceed one-half of the amount of the individual's support" (26 U.S.C. 1, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section1&num=0&edition=2024). At EXACTLY half of support the two readings disagree: the statute bars the refundable credit and i8863's wording let the filer answer No and keep it — an over-claim at that one boundary value. The sibling attestation form8615:/writableForm8615EarnedIncomeNotMoreThanHalfSupport already carries the statutory boundary for the same section 1(g) population; its Description's note that the two tests "diverge at that one boundary value and are kept separate rather than shared" describes the pre-correction state of this fact. Nothing computed moves: the path, the type, the unanswered-TRUE default and every consumer are unchanged; only what the application asks changes.

Fact.Name: Whether the primary filer's day-before-DOB age is complete
Fact.Description: Complete-safe probe for the Form 8863 refundable-credit age gate. The primary filer is selected from the complete /filers collection, so the gate can preserve its TRUE (barred) fallback without reading /primaryFiler directly in a computation arm.

Fact.Name: Complete-safe Form 8863 line 7 age condition 1
Refundable AOTC barred by the Form 8863 line 7 age test
Fact.Description:
TRUE when i8863 Line 7's conditions 1(a|b|c) AND 2 AND 3 all hold, in which case the filer "cannot claim any part of the American opportunity credit as a refundable credit" — line 8 is skipped and the whole of line 7 goes to line 9 as NONREFUNDABLE. The credit is NOT lost: it moves from Form 1040 line 29 to Schedule 3 line 3, where it offsets tax instead of being paid out.
FULL-TIME STUDENT (condition 1c) is read from /aotcFilerIsStudent, which reads the dedicated /writableAotcFilerFullTimeStudent attestation rather than the bare filers:/primaryFiler/isStudent Boolean. See /writableAotcFilerFullTimeStudent for detail.
AGE CONVENTION: all five age reads in this gate — the completeness guard and conditions 1(a), 1(b) and 1(c) — read filers:/primaryFiler/ageCalculatedDayBeforeDOB, the day-before-the-birthday convention, and no longer the anniversary-rule filers:/primaryFiler/age. IRC 25A(i)'s last sentence turns the refundable credit off only for a taxpayer who is a child to whom section 1(g) applies, and the IRS states the section 1(g) age on the day-before convention: "a child born on January 1, 2002, is considered to be age 24 at the end of 2025" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 36). form8615:/mustFileForm8615 already reads the same fact for the same section 1(g) population, and its own Description records the convention. Without the day-before convention a January-1-born filer would be one year younger to this gate than to the law, so condition 1(c) would bar a refundable credit the statute allows — an UNDER-claim, at the January-1 birthdays of 2002, 2007 and 2008.

Fact.Name: Filer was a full-time student for 2025 (Form 8863 line 7, condition 1c)
Fact.Description: Screen question, matching i8863's own interactive Line 7 worksheet question 3 verbatim: "Were you a full-time student for 2025?" Help text, paraphrasing i8863's "Full-time student" definition: you were a full-time student for 2025 if during any part of any 5 calendar months during the year you were enrolled as a full-time student at an eligible educational institution, or took a full-time, on-farm training course given by such an institution or by a state, county, or local government agency. Asked-when: only reached when the filer is under 24 at the end of 2025, on a non-joint return (i8863 Line 7 conditions 3 and the age-24 gate) — the same population /aotcRefundableBarredByAgeGate already screens for age. Unanswered posture: defaults to TRUE (the credit is barred), disclosed below — the World-#1-safe direction, since TRUE only ever makes the refundable credit LESS available, never pays out cash the statute bars. Validation: Boolean. Feeds /aotcRefundableBarredByAgeGate's condition 1(c) limb, which bars ONLY the REFUNDABLE portion — a barred filer's credit is not lost, it moves to line 9 (nonrefundable).

Fact.Name: Filer was a full-time student for 2025, with the absent-answer default applied (Form 8863 line 7, condition 1c)
Fact.Description:
/writableAotcFilerFullTimeStudent for the primary filer, defaulting to TRUE when unanswered. Guarded for the same reason the gate itself is (see the complete-safety note on /aotcRefundableBarredByAgeGate): a raw read of an unanswered writable resolves Incomplete and would cascade through the whole AOTC chain, flipping /aotcRefundableAmount and /sched3Line3 to Placeholder. TRUE is again the World-#1-safe default: it makes condition 1(c) fire, which BARS the refundable credit, which can only under-claim.
FULL-TIME READ. This fact reads the dedicated /writableAotcFilerFullTimeStudent attestation, matching i8863's own full-time definition (any part of any 5 calendar months). The bare filers:/primaryFiler/isStudent Boolean ("whether the filer is a student", no full-time qualifier) is a SUPERSET of that test: read here, it would make condition 1(c) fire for every student, part-time included, and bar the refundable credit for a part-time student aged 19-23 who met the other conditions (an under-claim of up to $1,000 of cash refund). The flow must ask the full-time question.

Fact.Name: Earned income less than half of support, with the absent-answer default applied
Fact.Description: /writableAotcEarnedIncomeLessThanHalfSupport, defaulting to TRUE when unanswered (the World-#1-safe direction — see the ABSENT-ANSWER POLICY note above). Split out so both condition 1(b) and condition 1(c) read one fact rather than duplicating the guard.

Fact.Name: Refundable American Opportunity Credit (Form 8863 line 8 → Form 1040 line 29)
Fact.Description:
Form 8863 Part I line 8 = 40% of line 7 (the refundable portion of the AOTC), reported on Form 1040 line 29. Feeds /americanOpportunityCredit. Complete-safe 0 when no AOTC.
ZERO when /aotcRefundableBarredByAgeGate — the form's own line-7 caution ("skip line 8"). Mechanically, /aotcNonrefundableAmount is line 7 − line 8, so barring line 8 pushes the FULL line 7 onto line 9 (Schedule 3 line 3), exactly as the form directs ("enter the amount from line 7 on line 9").
BUT DO NOT SAY "THE CREDIT MOVES, THE TAXPAYER KEEPS IT" — THAT IS FALSE. Line 9 is NONREFUNDABLE: it is capped by the filer's tax capacity, and §25A carries nothing forward, so every dollar of it above the filer's tax is simply LOST. The gated population is precisely the low-tax-capacity one, so the loss is typical, not exotic. Worked on a test fixture (single, $30,000 of wages → tax $1,475; AOTC $2,500): - without the gate: $1,000 refunded in cash + $1,475 of tax wiped out = $2,475 of benefit; - with the gate: $0 refunded + $1,475 of tax wiped out = $1,475 of benefit; - and $1,025 of the credit evaporates against a tax bill too small to absorb it. The taxpayer is $1,000 worse off. That is not a side effect to be softened — it is the ENTIRE POINT of the statute: Congress barred the refundable AOTC for these filers precisely so that it cannot be paid out as cash. Our job is to state that plainly, not to describe the fix in language that makes it sound costless.

Fact.Name: Nonrefundable American Opportunity Credit (Form 8863 line 9 → Credit Limit Worksheet line 2)
Fact.Description: Form 8863 Part I line 9 = line 7 − line 8 (the nonrefundable 60% of the AOTC), carried through the Credit Limit Worksheet to Form 8863 line 19 → Schedule 3 line 3. Computed as line 7 − line 8 (exact subtraction, not an independent 60% rounding). Complete-safe 0 when no AOTC. This is worksheet line 2, NOT the amount that reaches Schedule 3 — it feeds /form8863CreditLimitWorksheetLine3 and is then capped at remaining tax capacity by /nonrefundableEducationCredits (worksheet line 7). It does not feed /sched3Line3 directly.

Fact.Name: Adjusted qualified education expenses for the Lifetime Learning Credit (Form 8863 line 10)
Fact.Description: The total adjusted qualified education expenses for the Lifetime Learning Credit — Form 8863 Part II line 10 (the sum of Part III line 31 across students), supplied directly as a taxpayer input. The LLC is 20% of up to $10,000 of these expenses (max $2,000 per return). Complete-safe: 0 / unanswered ⇒ no LLC ⇒ /sched3Line3 unchanged. MFS filers are ineligible (credit 0). The per-student breakdown is still not modeled — this is Part II line 10, the total of every Part III line 31 on the return. The AOTC/LLC same-student exclusion of IRC 25A(c)(2)(A) is modeled through the attestation /writableLlcExpensesIncludeAotcStudent and the gate /llcAotcSameStudentCoordinationMet, which ask whose expenses this total holds because no per-student collection can say. Neither that gate nor /llcIdentificationMet reads an answered $0 as a claim, which is what keeps the Complete-safe promise above true in BOTH directions.

Fact.Name: The education credit expenses leave out every expense deducted elsewhere on this return
Fact.Description: Do the adjusted qualified education expenses you entered for the American opportunity credit (Form 8863 Part III line 27) and for the lifetime learning credit (Form 8863 Part II line 10) leave out every expense that you or the student also deducted on this return, for example as a business expense on Schedule C? An expense deducted anywhere else cannot also be used to figure an education credit. Asked when either expense amount is more than zero. Answering no blocks the return from being submitted until the expense amounts are corrected. UNANSWERED IS DEFAULTED: the amounts are used as entered and nothing is blocked, so an unasked question leaves the double benefit undetected.

Fact.Name: An education credit is claimed on expenses the filer says were also deducted elsewhere
Fact.Description: You said the education expenses you entered include expenses that you or the student also deducted elsewhere on this return, such as on Schedule C. Those expenses cannot also be used for an education credit. Remove them from the American opportunity credit expenses (Form 8863 line 27) and the lifetime learning credit expenses (Form 8863 line 10), then answer the question again. TRUE when /writableEducationExpensesExcludeAmountsDeductedElsewhere is answered no and either expense amount is more than zero; complete false otherwise, including when the question is unanswered. A submission block for a contradiction in the filer's own answers, not a scope refusal.

Fact.Name: Lifetime Learning Credit before phaseout (Form 8863 line 12)
Fact.Description: Form 8863 Part II line 12 = 20% × min(qualified expenses, $10,000), max $2,000. Gated on /writableLlcQualifiedExpenses answered AND the filer not being married-filing-separately (MFS is ineligible) AND Not(/educationCreditFilerCanBeClaimedAsDependent) (IRC 25A(g)(3)(A): a filer claimable as a dependent gets no education credit) AND /llcIdentificationMet (IRC 25A(g)(1)(A): the Part III student's name and TIN are a condition of allowance for this credit too) AND /llcAotcSameStudentCoordinationMet (IRC 25A(c)(2)(A): no LLC for expenses of a student for whom the AOTC is allowed) AND /llcPayeeStatementMet (IRC 25A(g)(8): the Form 1098-T condition, or an exception the Secretary provides); complete-safe 0 otherwise, except that an unanswered Part III name or TIN on a CLAIMING return leaves the identification gate — and so this line — Incomplete rather than a silent $0, which is the posture /aotcIdentificationAndPayeeStatementMet already carries on the AOTC side. The coordination gate carries the same posture for a same-student YES: the credit goes Incomplete so the AOTC student's expenses can be taken off line 10, because (c)(2)(A) removes only that student's expenses and this module cannot split the cross-student total. BOTH gates read a CLAIM as line 10 answered ABOVE ZERO — an answered $0 leaves this line Complete 0.00 and /sched3Line3 untouched. Rounded to whole dollars.

Fact.Name: Lifetime Learning Credit after MAGI phaseout (Form 8863 line 18 → Credit Limit Worksheet line 1)
Fact.Description: Form 8863 Part II line 18 = LLC before phaseout × clamp((threshold − MAGI)/range, 0, 1), with the same $90k/$180k threshold and $10k/$20k range as the AOTC (reuses /aotcPhaseoutThreshold + /aotcPhaseoutRange). MAGI is /form8863Magi, as on line 7. Line 18 reads the printed line 17 (/llcPhaseoutFractionThousandths, the 3-decimal ratio carried as integer thousandths) and divides by 1,000 only after the multiply, so the printed line 17 and the printed line 18 foot against each other exactly as "Multiply line 12 by line 17" says they must; the same canon /aotcCreditAfterPhaseout carries for lines 6 and 7. Nonrefundable. This is Credit Limit Worksheet line 1 — it adds to the AOTC nonrefundable amount at /form8863CreditLimitWorksheetLine3 (worksheet line 3), which is then capped at remaining tax capacity by /nonrefundableEducationCredits (worksheet line 7 = Form 8863 line 19) before reaching /sched3Line3. Complete-safe 0 when /form8863Magi is incomplete or the LLC is 0.

Fact.Name: Return has Form 8863 education credit inputs
Fact.Description: True when either Form 8863 expense input is answered (the AOTC adjusted qualified expenses or the Lifetime Learning Credit qualified expenses). Gates /nonrefundableEducationCredits so a return with no education expenses takes the else-0 branch WITHOUT evaluating the tax-capacity chain — keeping /sched3Line3 and /line8OfSchedule3 byte-identical on scenarios whose tax/credit facts are Placeholder or Incomplete (the branch-gate idiom, as used by form8396 /mortgageInterestCreditIsActive).

Fact.Name: Education Credit Limit Worksheet line 3 (total nonrefundable education credit before the limit)
Fact.Description: Form 8863 Line 19 Credit Limit Worksheet line 3 = line 1 (Form 8863 line 18, the Lifetime Learning Credit after phaseout) + line 2 (Form 8863 line 9, the nonrefundable AOTC). It is one arm of the smaller-of at line 7. Both terms are complete-safe 0.

Fact.Name: Education Credit Limit Worksheet line 5 (credits ordered before the education credit)
Fact.Description:
Form 8863 Line 19 Credit Limit Worksheet line 5 = the total of the credits on Schedule 3 (Form 1040) lines 1, 2, 6d and 6l — the credits applied against tax BEFORE the nonrefundable education credit. In this dictionary Schedule 3 line 2 is cdcc /cdccTotalCredit and line 6d is elderlyAndDisabled /totalEdc (neither has a dedicated /sched3Line* fact); this is the same mapping form8396.xml uses for its own worksheet line 2. The printed set EXCLUDES Schedule 3 line 3 itself and the CTC/ODC, which is exactly why this chain is acyclic — see the section note above.
EVERY TERM IS IsComplete-GATED, and that is load-bearing, not decorative. The worksheet says "Enter the total of your CREDITS from ..." — a credit the return does not take contributes nothing, so an unresolved term enters 0. Without the gates a return that HAS education expenses but whose CDCC or Schedule R facts sit at Placeholder drags this fact, /form8863TaxLiabilityLimit, /nonrefundableEducationCredits and finally /sched3Line3 to Incomplete — i.e. Schedule 3 line 3 DISAPPEARS from a return that is owed an education credit. That was measured on a probe scenario (a form2441 CDCC case plus AOTC expenses), not theorised; no scenario in the committed corpus reaches it, so the strict delta check would not have caught it. This is the "only if allowed and taken" gate form8396.xml applies to its own CTC term, applied to all four terms here.

Fact.Name: Education Credit Limit Worksheet line 6 (tax capacity remaining for the education credit)
Fact.Description: Form 8863 Line 19 Credit Limit Worksheet line 6 = line 4 (Form 1040 line 18, taxCalculations /totalTentativeTax) minus line 5 (/form8863CreditLimitWorksheetLine5), floored at 0.

Fact.Name: Nonrefundable education credits (Form 8863 line 19 → Schedule 3 line 3)
Fact.Description: Form 8863 line 19 = Credit Limit Worksheet line 7 = the smaller of worksheet line 3 (/form8863CreditLimitWorksheetLine3, the AOTC nonrefundable + LLC total) and worksheet line 6 (/form8863TaxLiabilityLimit, the tax remaining after the credits ordered first), ROUNDED to whole dollars at this line (the convention: a fact standing for a printed entry line rounds AT that line). Flows to /sched3Line3 → /line8OfSchedule3 → Form 1040 line 20. Complete-safe: with no Form 8863 expense input the else branch yields 0 WITHOUT evaluating the limit chain, so every scenario without an education credit keeps /sched3Line3, /line8OfSchedule3 and total tax byte-identical.

Fact.Name: Form 8862 is required for the American Opportunity Credit
Fact.Description: Whether the taxpayer must file Form 8862 to claim the American Opportunity Credit, because the credit was denied in an earlier year through the deficiency procedures and the Secretary requires the recertification before it may be claimed again. The twin of eitc:/eitc8862Required and ctcOdc:/ctc8862Required, which the register already prints at Form 8862 line 2's first two boxes; it gates every Part IV box. A writable rather than a derivation because the graph has no AOTC deficiency-procedure intake to derive from: there is no AOTC counterpart of /eitcReceivedImproperClaimsNotice or /receivedImproperClaimsNotice. (The graph does carry an AOTC prior-claim intake, /writableAotcPriorFraudOrRecklessDisregardDetermination, but that one is IRC 25A(b)(4)(A), the absolute disallowance period no form lifts, and not the IRC 25A(b)(4)(B) recertification this fact models, so it cannot derive this one.) Print only until /pdfIncludeForm8862 consumes it: that fact is today the OR of the EIC and CTC triggers alone, so an AOTC only Form 8862 does not yet render. It DOES have a fact graph consumer: /aotcStudentEligibleForAotc reads it as the switch on the Form 8862 Part IV limb of the American Opportunity Credit eligibility gate, deliberately as Any(Not(answered AND true), the 19a/19b test) so that an unanswered recertification question does not bar the credit.

Fact.Name: Form 8862 AOTC requirement, complete-safe Boolean
Fact.Description: Passes the Form 8862 requirement through when answered and supplies false when the intake is unanswered, so the line 18a student-name switch takes its existing empty fallthrough without turning an unanswered gate into an incomplete PDF value.

Fact.Name: Form 8863 Part III line 28 is zero
Fact.Description: The complement of /aotcExpensesExceedFirstTier: line 28 is zero, which is the condition Form 8863 Part III line 30 tests by name. Because line 28 is floored at zero it can never be negative, so not greater than zero means exactly zero. Incompleteness propagates through Not, which is what keeps line 30 blank when line 27 is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Form 8863 Part III line 28 is more than zero
Fact.Description: Whether line 28, /aotcExpensesOverFirstTier, is greater than zero. The selector Form 8863 Part III line 30 turns on, stated in the positive so the Not below can read it: line 30 says "If line 28 is zero, enter the amount from line 27. Otherwise ...", and because line 28 is floored at zero, not zero and greater than zero are the same condition. Not printed; it exists to drive /aotcPerStudentTentativeCredit.

Fact.Name: Adjusted qualified education expenses over the first $2,000 (Form 8863 Part III line 28)
Fact.Description: Form 8863 Part III line 28 as printed: "Subtract $2,000 from line 27. If zero or less, enter -0-", that is the greater of /aotcExpensesOverFirstTierRaw and zero. Line 27 is /writableAotcQualifiedExpenses. GATED exactly as line 30 (/aotcPerStudentTentativeCredit) and Part I line 1 are: all three read /aotcCreditAllowedForThisFilerAndStudent, so a filer or student barred from the credit prints $0 on lines 28, 29 and 30 rather than a nonzero line 28 and line 29 beside a $0 line 30. Line 27 unanswered stays Incomplete rather than $0, so the line stays blank for a lifetime-learning-only student whose Part III line 27 is blank. The arithmetic matches the credit /aotcTentativeCredit computes: $2,000 is a whole number, so the rounded line 29 composes into the same line 30.

Fact.Name: Adjusted qualified education expenses over the first $2,000, before the zero floor (Form 8863 line 28 step)
Fact.Description: Line 27 minus $2,000, the raw subtraction Form 8863 Part III line 28 asks for before its "If zero or less, enter -0-" instruction is applied. Split out from the floored line because a subtract and a greater of are two templates; the printed line is /aotcExpensesOverFirstTier, which floors this value at zero. This helper may be NEGATIVE and is not printed anywhere. Complete exactly when /writableAotcQualifiedExpenses is.

Fact.Name: American Opportunity Credit first tier expense limit (Form 8863 line 28 and line 30 constant)
Fact.Description: The $2,000 printed on Form 8863 Part III line 28, "Subtract $2,000 from line 27", and again on line 30, "add $2,000 to the amount on line 29", named as a fact so those two printed lines can be built from Dollar facts rather than from a literal buried inside a larger expression. The amount is the statutory first tier ceiling of IRC 25A(b)(1)(A) and already carries a param ledger id in this repo: authority/ty2025/parameters.tsv records aotc-first-tier-expense-limit for 8863 lines 28 and 30 at 2000, and dictionary/ty2025/form8863.xml tags both of its inline copies of the same constant with that id inside /aotcTentativeCredit. This fact names it once instead of a third and fourth time inline.

Fact.Name: $2,000 added to the Form 8863 line 29 amount (Form 8863 line 30, otherwise arm)
Fact.Description: The "otherwise" arm of Form 8863 Part III line 30: $2,000 added to the amount on line 29, that is /aotcSecondTierCreditAmount plus /aotcFirstTierExpenseLimitAmount. Split out because the switch template selects between two Dollar FACTS, so the arm needs a name. Not printed by itself; /aotcPerStudentTentativeCredit chooses between it and line 27.

Fact.Name: Hope Scholarship Credit or AOTC was not claimed for the student for 4 prior tax years
Fact.Description: The complement of /writableAotcClaimedForFourPriorTaxYears, split out so the Form 8862 line 19b No box reads one fact rather than repeating the negation.

Fact.Name: Tentative American Opportunity Credit for this student (Form 8863 Part III line 30)
Fact.Description: Form 8863 Part III line 30 as printed: if line 28 is zero, the amount from line 27, otherwise $2,000 added to the amount on line 29. The condition is /aotcExpensesAtOrBelowFirstTier, the line 27 arm is /aotcQualifiedExpensesAtLeastZero and the other arm is /aotcFirstTierPlusSecondTierCredit. GATED, exactly as Form 8863 Part I line 1 is: both read /aotcCreditAllowedForThisFilerAndStudent, so a filer or student barred from the credit prints $0 here too rather than a credit at line 30 against $0 at line 1. Line 27 unanswered stays Incomplete rather than $0, matching what a filer who never claims the American Opportunity Credit for this student leaves blank on the printed page; see /aotcCreditAllowedForThisFilerAndStudent for why that one axis still legitimately divides this fact from /aotcTentativeCredit.

Fact.Name: 25 percent of the expenses over the first $2,000 (Form 8863 Part III line 29)
Fact.Description: Form 8863 Part III line 29, "Multiply line 28 by 25% (0.25)": 25 hundredths of /aotcExpensesOverFirstTier, computed with the pro rata template over the structural rate pair /aotcSecondTierRateNumerator and /aotcSecondTierRateDenominator. The template rounds to whole dollars, which is what /aotcTentativeCredit already does to the sum this line feeds; because the $2,000 line 30 adds to it is a whole number, rounding here and rounding the total agree to the cent. Complete exactly when line 28 is: the template's zero arm is unreachable here because its whole is a complete positive literal. Because line 28 is $0 for a filer or student barred from the credit (/aotcCreditAllowedForThisFilerAndStudent false), this line is $0 there too.

Fact.Name: Denominator of the Form 8863 line 29 second tier rate (structural, 25 of 100)
Fact.Description: The 100 of the percent in the "25% (0.25)" printed on Form 8863 Part III line 29, as a Dollar fact, so the rate can be applied with the pro rata template. It is also the completeness guard of that template: the whole is a literal, always complete and always greater than zero, so /aotcSecondTierCreditAmount is complete exactly when line 28 is and never falls through to the template's zero arm. Structural: a rate encoding, not a statutory dollar figure. The twin of the promoted /form5329PercentRateDenominator, which does the same job for the 6, 10 and 25 percent rates printed on Form 5329.

Fact.Name: Numerator of the Form 8863 line 29 second tier rate (structural, 25 of 100)
Fact.Description: The 25 of the "25% (0.25)" printed on Form 8863 Part III line 29, as a Dollar fact. The supported templates express multiplication only as a pro rata share, Round(total times part divided by whole), so a rate has to be encoded as a pair of Dollar facts; this is the part and /aotcSecondTierRateDenominator is the whole. Structural rather than a param ledger amount: it is a rate encoding, not a dollar figure. The rate itself is statutory, the 25 percent of IRC 25A(b)(1)(B). The shape is already promoted and engine validated elsewhere in this dictionary: dictionary/ty2025/form5329.xml carries /form5329SixPercentRateNumerator, /form5329TenPercentRateNumerator and /form5329PercentRateDenominator for exactly this reason, and every Form 5329 additional tax line resolves as Round(base times numerator divided by 100).

Fact.Name: Student did not complete the first 4 years of postsecondary education before 2025 (Form 8863 line 25 No box)
Fact.Description: The No box of the Form 8863 line 25 pair, the answer that continues to line 26: Not(/writableAotcStudentCompletedFirstFourYears). A checkbox mapping names one Bool, so the No box needs its own fact; incompleteness propagates through Not, so an unanswered line 25 prints neither box.

Fact.Name: Student did not meet the eligible student requirements for the AOTC
Fact.Description: The complement of /writableAotcStudentIsEligibleStudent, split out so the Form 8862 line 19a No box reads one fact rather than repeating the negation, which is the shape dictionary/ty2025/eitc.xml uses for /pdf8862Line4Yes and /pdf8862Line4No.

Fact.Name: Student was not convicted of a felony drug offense before the end of 2025 (Form 8863 line 26 No box)
Fact.Description: The No box of the Form 8863 line 26 pair, the answer whose printed instruction is to complete lines 27 through 30 for this student: Not(/writableAotcStudentFelonyDrugConviction). A checkbox mapping names one Bool, so the No box needs its own fact; incompleteness propagates through Not, so an unanswered line 26 prints neither box.

Fact.Name: American Opportunity Credit was not claimed for this student for 4 prior tax years (Form 8863 line 23 No box)
Fact.Description: The No box of the Form 8863 line 23 pair, the answer that continues to line 24: Not(/writableAotcStudentClaimedForFourPriorTaxYears). A checkbox mapping names one Bool and takes its on state from the widget, so the No box needs its own fact; incompleteness propagates through Not, so an unanswered line 23 prints neither box.

Fact.Name: Student was not enrolled at least half time in 2025 (Form 8863 line 24 No box)
Fact.Description: The No box of the Form 8863 line 24 pair, the answer whose printed instruction is to stop and go to line 31 for this student: Not(/writableAotcStudentEnrolledAtLeastHalfTime). A checkbox mapping names one Bool and takes its on state from the widget, so the No box needs its own fact; incompleteness propagates through Not, so an unanswered line 24 prints neither box.

Fact.Name: MAGI headroom below the education credit phaseout threshold (Form 8863 lines 4 and 15)
Fact.Description:
Form 8863 line 4 (Part I, the American Opportunity Credit) and line 15 (Part II, the Lifetime Learning Credit): the phaseout threshold minus modified adjusted gross income. Both printed lines are the same subtraction over the same two facts, because this module reuses one threshold fact for both credits: line 2 and line 13 are both /aotcPhaseoutThreshold, and line 3 and line 14 are both /form8863Magi. The shipped register already prints /aotcPhaseoutThreshold on lines 2 and 13 and /aotcPhaseoutRange on lines 5 and 16, so one fact serving two printed lines is this form's established shape rather than a shortcut.
THE VALUE IS THE RAW SUBTRACTION AND MAY BE NEGATIVE, which is the reading the printed form supports. Line 4 says "Subtract line 3 from line 2. If zero or less, stop; you can't take any education credit" and line 15 says "Subtract line 14 from line 13. If zero or less, skip lines 16 and 17, enter -0- on line 18, and go to line 19". Neither line instructs the filer to enter -0- on ITSELF; line 15 puts its -0- on line 18. A zero-or-less result is a routing instruction, not a floor on the printed entry. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: flooring at 0, which would print a number the form does not ask for and would hide the very condition the two STOP instructions turn on. The module's own clamp of this quantity, GreaterOf(0, threshold minus MAGI) capped by the phaseout range, lives once in /educationCreditPhaseoutHeadroomFloored and the two ratio facts below it, which the two credit lines read rather than nesting an unnamed copy of the clamp; this fact is the printed line, not the clamp.
Complete exactly when /form8863Magi is, which is exactly when /agi is, so it adds no completeness surface of its own.

Fact.Name: Students listed on Form 8862 Part IV
Fact.Description: The students for whom the American Opportunity Credit is being recertified on Form 8862 Part IV. The printed part has three slots and its own instruction to attach a statement for a fourth student, so it quantifies over students; dictionary/pdf/2025/column-axes.tsv declares the register row IRS8862 /form8862AotcStudents rows 3. The shipping graph cannot supply them: dictionary/ty2025/form8863.xml scopes the American Opportunity Credit to one student, and no student collection exists anywhere in the manifest, so this is an intake, not a derivation. A writable Collection has items only when the flow adds a student, which is why the per item leaves need no separate recertification gate. PRINT ONLY until the obligation on this fact is met: nothing computes from these items, and the shipping student-1 scalars still print the line 18a, 19a and 19b Student 1 boxes.

Fact.Name: Student did not meet the eligible student requirements for the AOTC
Fact.Description: The complement of /form8862AotcStudents/*/writableIsEligibleStudent, one per student on Form 8862 Part IV. The line 19a No box needs its own Bool because a checkbox mapping names exactly one fact and the filler takes the on state from the widget; this is the per item form of the shipping single-student scalar /aotcStudentIsNotEligibleStudent. Incompleteness propagates through Not, so a student whose line 19a is unanswered prints neither box.

Fact.Name: Hope Scholarship Credit or AOTC was not claimed for this student for 4 prior tax years
Fact.Description: The complement of /form8862AotcStudents/*/writableClaimedForFourPriorTaxYears, one per student on Form 8862 Part IV, so the line 19b No box reads one fact rather than repeating the negation. This is the per item form of the shipping single-student scalar /aotcNotClaimedForFourPriorTaxYears. Incompleteness propagates through Not, so a student whose line 19b is unanswered prints neither box.

Fact.Name: Hope Scholarship Credit or AOTC was claimed for this student for 4 prior tax years
Fact.Description: One student's answer to Form 8862 line 19b: whether the Hope Scholarship Credit or the American Opportunity Credit has been claimed for this student for any 4 tax years before the year entered on line 1. A writable because the graph keeps no prior year credit history for a student. TRUE fills that student's Yes box, which the printed Caution says bars the credit for that student; the No box is the sibling /form8862AotcStudents/*/notClaimedForFourPriorTaxYears. Item [1] prints the Student 2 pair and item [2] the Student 3 pair; the Student 1 pair stays on the shipping single-student scalars until the collection obligation on /form8862AotcStudents is met. Print only: no computation consumes it.

Fact.Name: Student met the eligible student requirements for the AOTC
Fact.Description: One student's answer to Form 8862 line 19a: whether the student met the requirements to be an eligible student for purposes of the American Opportunity Credit for the year entered on line 1. A writable: Form 8862 asks the taxpayer directly. The Form 8863 Part III tests that decide the credit are /aotcStudentEligibleForAotc; this answer is printed and is not reconciled with them. TRUE fills that student's Yes box; the No box is the sibling /form8862AotcStudents/*/isNotEligibleStudent, and an unanswered question leaves both blank. Item [1] prints the Student 2 pair and item [2] the Student 3 pair; the Student 1 pair stays on the shipping single-student scalars until the collection obligation on /form8862AotcStudents is met. Print only: no computation consumes it.

Fact.Name: Name of a student listed on Form 8862 Part IV
Fact.Description: The name of one student on Form 8862 Part IV, as listed on Form 8863, supplied directly by the taxpayer. Line 18 says "Enter the name(s) of the student(s) as listed on Form 8863" and prints three slots, 18a, 18b and 18c. The graph carries no student identity of its own: form8863.xml never names a student and Form 8863's own student name box prints the filer names, so this is an intake. Item [1] prints line 18b and item [2] prints line 18c; item [0] prints line 18a once the collection obligation on /form8862AotcStudents is met, and until then line 18a stays on the shipping single-student scalar /pdf8862Line18aStudentName. Print only: no computation consumes it.

Fact.Name: Student did not receive a 2025 Form 1098-T from the first institution (Form 8863 line 22a)
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 8863 Part III line 22a(2). A checkbox mapping names one Bool and the filler sets the box when that Bool is true, so the No box needs a fact of its own: this is Not(/writableForm8863FirstInstitutionCurrentYear1098T). Incompleteness propagates through Not, so an unanswered question leaves the No box blank as well as the Yes box, and the pair can never both print.

Fact.Name: Student did not receive a 2024 Form 1098-T with box 7 checked from the first institution (Form 8863 line 22a)
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 8863 Part III line 22a(3): Not(/writableForm8863FirstInstitutionPriorYear1098TBox7). Same shape and same reasoning as the line 22a(2) pair: a checkbox mapping names one Bool, so the No box needs its own fact, and incompleteness propagates through Not so an unanswered question prints neither box.

Fact.Name: The Secretary's Form 1098-T exception applies (first institution)
Fact.Description: Screen question: "You said you did not receive a Form 1098-T from this institution. Does one of these exceptions apply to you?" Asked only when the student answered No to receiving a 2025 Form 1098-T from the first institution (/form8863FirstInstitutionNoCurrentYear1098T is true) and No to receiving a 2024 Form 1098-T from it with box 7 checked. Help text, paraphrasing the Instructions for Form 8863's "Form 1098-T requirement" section: you may still claim an education credit without a Form 1098-T if EITHER (1) the institution was not required to furnish one — for example the student is a qualified nonresident alien, paid qualified education expenses entirely with scholarships, paid under a formal billing arrangement, or was enrolled only in courses for which no academic credit is awarded — and you can demonstrate the student was enrolled at an eligible institution and substantiate the payment of qualified expenses; OR (2) the institution was required to furnish one but the student did not receive it before you file, and after January 31, 2026 you (or the student) requested it from the institution, fully cooperated with the institution's efforts to furnish it, and can otherwise substantiate the claim. Answer Yes only when one of these two paths applies. Unanswered posture: the education credit is refused for this student (computed $0, section 25A(g)(8) reason disclosed) — the payee-statement requirement is a condition of allowance the statute states categorically ("except as otherwise provided by the Secretary"), so an unaddressed No answer cannot default to allowing the credit. Validation: Boolean. Feeds /aotcFirstInstitutionPayeeStatementMet, which gates /aotcTentativeCredit and, through /llcPayeeStatementMet, /llcCreditBeforePhaseout.

Fact.Name: The IRC 25A(g)(8) payee-statement condition is met for the first institution
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the student received a 2025 Form 1098-T from the first institution (line 22a(2) Yes), OR received a 2024 Form 1098-T from it with box 7 checked (line 22a(3) Yes), OR received neither but the taxpayer attests that one of i8863's own carve-outs applies (/writableForm8863First1098TExceptionApplies).
LINE 22a(3) SATISFIES THE STATEMENT REQUIREMENT. Section 25A(g)(8) asks for "a statement furnished under section 6050S(d)" and does not tie it to the tax year; a 2024 Form 1098-T with box 7 checked is such a statement from this institution and reports amounts for an academic period beginning in the first three months of 2025. The form asks (3) beside (2) and requires the EIN "if you checked Yes in (2) or (3)", treating the two as alternatives. The expense entry still takes only amounts paid in 2025: payments made in 2024 cannot be used in 2025 (i8863 Prepaid Expenses), and that is the expense intake's rule, not this gate's. The reading is recorded in dictionary/ty2025/TAX-INTERPRETATIONS-FOR-EXPERT-REVIEW.md (CR-11). Section 25A(g)(8) makes receiving the statement a condition of allowance for BOTH education credits ("no credit shall be allowed under THIS SECTION"), but the module has no LLC-specific 1098-T intake (Form 8863 Part II carries no institution boxes of its own; every 1098-T fact here is scoped to the Part III AOTC student), so this gate reads into /aotcTentativeCredit directly, and the LLC side of (g)(8) reads it through /llcPayeeStatementMet, which applies it only when Part II line 10 is a claim.
UNANSWERED 1098-T RECEIPT QUESTION IS INCOMPLETE, NOT COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: the receipt question is read directly, not wrapped in IsComplete, so a claiming return that has never been asked "did you receive a Form 1098-T" leaves this fact — and so /aotcIdentificationAndPayeeStatementMet and /aotcTentativeCredit — Incomplete rather than silently filing a $0 AOTC. Once the receipt question IS answered No, the exception sub-clause keeps its own COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE idiom, "IsComplete(x) AND (value test)" as two conjuncts, unchanged: an answered "No, and I don't attest to an exception" still bars the credit deterministically, the way the statute's condition of allowance requires — this is the ANSWERED-missing case, distinct from the never-asked case above.

Fact.Name: IRC 25A(g)(1) identification and (g)(8) payee-statement conditions of allowance are met
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the student's name and TIN are both on the return (g(1)(A)), the first institution's EIN is on the return (g(1)(B)(iii), AOTC-specific — Form 8863 Part II prints no institution box, so this leg does not apply to the LLC), and the first institution's payee-statement condition is met (g(8), /aotcFirstInstitutionPayeeStatementMet). Gates /aotcTentativeCredit only, for the reason each leg states: name/TIN and EIN are collected at Part III (the AOTC per-student worksheet), and no LLC-scoped identification or 1098-T fact exists in this dictionary.
WHAT THIS FACT DOES NOT TEST: (1) IRC 25A(g)(1)(B)(i)/(ii), the student's and taxpayer's TIN must have been ISSUED by the return's due date. That condition is the separate bar /aotcBarredByTinIssuedAfterDueDate, read beside this fact by /aotcCreditAllowedForThisFilerAndStudent; this fact tests only that a TIN was SUPPLIED. (2) The second institution's own EIN and 1098-T conditions are only partly gated here. Its EIN IS gated, by the same unanswered-is-Incomplete posture as the first institution's, but ONLY when IsComplete(/writableForm8863SecondInstitutionName): a second institution is optional on the form ("if any"), and IRC 25A(g)(1)(B)(iii) asks for the EIN of any institution the expenses were paid to. The second institution's 1098-T pair does not enter this fact: whether IRC 25A(g)(8)'s single "statement" must come from EACH institution is a reading the statute does not settle, so a named second institution with no statement refuses the return (/knockoutSecondInstitutionWithoutForm1098T). (3) The LLC's own (g)(1)(A) name/TIN condition is built, in its own fact /llcIdentificationMet, which reads the same Part III line 20/21 boxes this fact reads — the form completes ONE Part III per student for whom EITHER credit is claimed, so at this module's single-student scope those two boxes identify the LLC student as well. The LLC's (g)(8) payee-statement condition is built in /llcPayeeStatementMet, which reads /aotcFirstInstitutionPayeeStatementMet on a return whose Part II line 10 is a claim.
NO SILENT $0 ON AN UNASKED RETURN: a return that never claims the AOTC at all (no qualified expenses entered for this student) leaves this fact TRUE — the identification questions were never relevant, so there is nothing to disclose as unfinished. A return that DOES claim the AOTC and has fully answered name, TIN and institution EIN resolves the deterministic value (name/TIN/EIN present AND the payee statement condition met). A return that claims the AOTC but has NOT fully answered name, TIN or institution EIN resolves Incomplete rather than a silent Complete FALSE — the return is disclosed as unfinished, not filed with a $0 credit. The payee-statement leg carries its own unanswered-vs-answered split (see /aotcFirstInstitutionPayeeStatementMet): a never-asked 1098-T receipt question is Incomplete on a claiming return; an ANSWERED "No 1098-T, no exception" still bars the credit deterministically, since that condition of allowance was actually adjudicated, not skipped.

Fact.Name: IRC 25A(g)(1)(A) identification condition of allowance is met for the Lifetime Learning Credit
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the name and the taxpayer identification number of the student whose expenses Form 8863 Part II line 10 carries are both on the return. Section 25A(g)(1)(A) allows NO credit "under subsection (a)" unless the taxpayer includes the individual's name and TIN, and subsection (a) is both (a)(1), the American Opportunity Credit, and (a)(2), the Lifetime Learning Credit, so this condition reaches the LLC exactly as it reaches the AOTC.
WHICH NAME AND TIN. This module declares a SINGLE-STUDENT Part III scope, and the form's own caution above line 20 says to complete a Part III "for each student for whom you're claiming either the American opportunity credit or lifetime learning credit". The one Part III this module models therefore identifies the one student either credit is claimed for, and its line 20 and line 21 boxes are /writableAotcStudentName and /writableAotcStudentTin. Those two paths are named for the AOTC because the AOTC module was built first; they hold the Part III student's identity, not an AOTC-only pair.
WHAT THIS FACT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CARRY. (1) No institution EIN leg: IRC 25A(g)(1)(B)(iii) is an ADDITIONAL requirement stated "with respect to the American Opportunity Tax Credit" only, and Form 8863 line 22a(4) asks for the EIN "if you're claiming the American opportunity credit or if you checked Yes in (2) or (3)", so an LLC-only return that received no Form 1098-T is never asked for one. (2) No payee-statement leg: IRC 25A(g)(8) bars a credit "under this section", which reaches the Lifetime Learning Credit as squarely as it reaches the AOTC, and it is built in its own fact, /llcPayeeStatementMet, which reads line 22a(2)'s 1098-T answer on the same Part III this fact reads. (3) No TIN-issuance timing: (g)(1)(B)(i) and (ii) are AOTC-only, and no TIN-issue-date fact exists anywhere in this dictionary.
UNANSWERED POSTURE, the split /aotcIdentificationAndPayeeStatementMet already uses. A return that claims no Lifetime Learning Credit at all leaves this TRUE: the identification questions were never relevant. NO CLAIM MEANS PART II LINE 10 UNANSWERED **OR ANSWERED ZERO** — a $0 line 10 asks for no credit, so making it open the identification condition would leave /sched3Line3 Incomplete on a return that claims nothing, which is exactly what /writableLlcQualifiedExpenses's own "Complete-safe: 0 / unanswered" promise forbids. A claiming return (line 10 above zero) with both boxes answered resolves TRUE deterministically. A claiming return with either box unanswered falls off the Switch and resolves Incomplete, so the return is disclosed as unfinished rather than filed with a silent $0 Lifetime Learning Credit.

Fact.Name: IRC 25A(g)(8) payee-statement condition of allowance is met for the Lifetime Learning Credit
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the Lifetime Learning Credit may be allowed under the Form 1098-T condition. Section 25A(g)(8) allows NO credit "under this section" unless the taxpayer receives the Form 1098-T statement, except as the Secretary otherwise provides, and "this section" is both credits. The Instructions for Form 8863 say the same thing of both credits by name: to claim the American opportunity credit OR the lifetime learning credit, the law requires the taxpayer (or a dependent) to have received Form 1098-T, subject to the Secretary's exceptions.
WHICH 1098-T ANSWER. Form 8863 asks the 1098-T question once, on Part III line 22a(2) of the student's own Part III, and a Part III is completed for every student for whom EITHER credit is claimed. This module models one Part III, so the answer it reads is the one /aotcFirstInstitutionPayeeStatementMet already combines: the line 22a(2) receipt answer, or, when that answer is No, the attestation that one of the Secretary's exceptions applies. That is the same single-student reading /llcIdentificationMet takes for the line 20 and 21 boxes. On a return whose AOTC is ALLOWED for the Part III student and whose line 10 holds only other students' expenses, the other students' receipt is not asked; the AOTC gate has already required this Part III's answer, so this fact can never bar such a return wrongly, it can only fail to test the other students. The per-student Part III collection is the shape that would test each of them.
UNANSWERED POSTURE, the split /llcIdentificationMet uses. No claim (line 10 unanswered, or answered at or below zero) is TRUE: the question was never relevant. A claiming return with the receipt question answered Yes, or No with the exception attested, is TRUE; No with the exception answered No is FALSE, and the credit is barred deterministically. A claiming return whose receipt question was never answered resolves Incomplete, so the return is disclosed as unfinished rather than filed with a silent $0 or a silent credit. Written as one Any rather than a Switch: Any short-circuits on its first Complete true leg, and with no true leg an Incomplete leg makes the whole Incomplete.

Fact.Name: The Part II line 10 total includes expenses of the student the American Opportunity Credit is claimed for
Fact.Description:
Screen question: "You're claiming the American opportunity credit for the student on this Form 8863. Do the lifetime learning credit expenses you entered include any expenses for that same student?" Help text carries the form's own two cautions verbatim: Form 8863 page 2 says "You can't take the American opportunity credit and the lifetime learning credit for the same student in the same year. If you complete lines 27 through 30 for this student, don't complete line 31", and the instructions' Table 1 says "You can claim both the American opportunity credit and the lifetime learning credit on the same return, but not for the same student." Yes means the AOTC student's expenses are inside the Part II line 10 total and have to come off it — the Lifetime Learning Credit stops as Incomplete until they do, it is NOT barred (see "A YES DOES NOT BAR THE CREDIT" below). No means the total belongs entirely to OTHER students, which is lawful and common, and the credit stands.
WHY THIS IS AN ATTESTATION AND NOT A DERIVATION. Form 8863 enforces the rule structurally: each student gets their own Part III, and that student's expenses go either to lines 27-30 (AOTC) or to line 31 (LLC), never both. This module models ONE Part III at return level and collects Part II line 10 — "the total of all amounts from all Parts III, line 31" — as a single writable that sums across students. With no per-student collection there is nothing in the graph that says whose expenses the line 10 total holds, so the one question the form's structure would have answered has to be asked. Building the per-student Part III collection is the long-run shape and would retire this writable; it needs a dictionary/pdf/2025/column-axes.tsv row for IRS8863 before Part III could be printed per student at all, which is why it is not done here.
ASKED-WHEN: only on a return that claims BOTH credits, i.e. /writableLlcQualifiedExpenses is answered ABOVE ZERO AND /aotcTentativeCredit is above zero (the AOTC actually survives every eligibility, dependency, MFS and identification gate for the Part III student) AND /aotcPhaseoutFractionThousandths is above zero (below the MAGI ceiling both credits are $0 and the answer cannot move a dollar). On every other return the question is moot and is never asked.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: on a return that claims both, /llcAotcSameStudentCoordinationMet — and so the Lifetime Learning Credit — resolves Incomplete, disclosing the return as unfinished. It does NOT default to allowing the credit, because that would be a silent double credit for one student, and it does not default to barring it, because that would silently take a lawful two-student return's credit away.
A YES DOES NOT BAR THE CREDIT — IT ASKS FOR LINE 10 TO BE FIXED. IRC 25A(c)(2)(A) removes the AOTC student's EXPENSES, not the other students' credit, and line 10 is a cross-student total this module cannot split. So a Yes routes /llcAotcSameStudentCoordinationMet to Incomplete and the screen must INSTRUCT REMOVAL: "Take that student's expenses out of the lifetime learning total — Form 8863 says if you complete lines 27 through 30 for a student, don't complete line 31 for that student. Any OTHER students' expenses stay." That is what the form does structurally by never putting those expenses on line 31, and it is the only answer that neither double-counts one student nor under-claims the others. Validation: Boolean.

Fact.Name: IRC 25A(c)(2)(A) coordination: the Part II line 10 expenses are not a student's whose AOTC is allowed
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the Lifetime Learning Credit may take the Form 8863 Part II line 10 expenses into account at all. IRC 25A(c)(2)(A) removes from the LLC the qualified tuition and related expenses "with respect to an individual who is an eligible student for whom a American Opportunity Tax Credit under subsection (a)(1) is allowed for the taxable year", and the form states the same rule twice on its own face: complete lines 27-30 for a student and don't complete line 31 for that student.
THE FOUR ARMS, and why each default is the one it is. (1) A return that enters no Part II line 10 total — or enters a zero one — claims no LLC, so there is nothing to coordinate and this is TRUE. An answered $0 is NOT a claim: it takes no expenses into account, so the statute has nothing to remove, and treating it as a claim would leave /sched3Line3 Incomplete on a return that asks for neither credit. (2) A return whose /aotcTentativeCredit is not above zero is a return for which no American Opportunity Credit is ALLOWED for the Part III student — either none was claimed, or one was claimed and barred by the dependency, MFS, student-eligibility or identification gates — and (c)(2)(A) only removes expenses of a student for whom the AOTC IS allowed, so this is TRUE as well. That second arm is what keeps the printed routing honest: Part III lines 23-26 each say "Stop! Go to line 31 for this student", which is the form itself sending a barred student's expenses to the Lifetime Learning Credit. (3) When both credits genuinely reach the student, an attestation of NO — the line 10 total holds only OTHER students' expenses — is TRUE. (4) At or above the MAGI ceiling the printed ratio (line 6, and its line 17 alias) is 0, so both credits are $0 and the question cannot move a dollar; the arm exists so an unanswered attestation does not leave the credit Incomplete on a return where it is zero either way. Everything else — a YES, or an unanswered attestation below the ceiling — resolves Incomplete.
WHY A YES IS INCOMPLETE AND NOT A BAR. IRC 25A(c)(2)(A) strikes "the qualified tuition and related expenses with respect to an individual" — it removes THAT STUDENT'S EXPENSES, not the whole Lifetime Learning Credit. Part II line 10 is a cross-student total (that is the only reason the attestation has to be asked at all), and this module cannot split it, so a Yes on a two-student return whose line 10 mixes the AOTC student's expenses with another student's would, if it barred the credit outright, ALSO take away the lawful student's credit. Routing a Yes to Incomplete is lawful on every return, because a correctly prepared Form 8863 never puts an AOTC student's expenses on line 31 in the first place — the form's own "If you complete lines 27 through 30 for this student, don't complete line 31" — so the honest response is to send the filer back to line 10 to remove them, not to guess at a number the return does not carry. The question's screen must say so. The per-student Part III collection would derive the split and let a Yes bar exactly the right expenses; it is the named successor to this fact.
WHY THE TEST IS ON LINE 1 AND NOT ON LINE 7: /aotcTentativeCredit is the AOTC before the MAGI phaseout, and it already carries every condition of allowance this module builds. Using the post-phaseout /aotcCreditAfterPhaseout instead could never change a dollar, because IRC 25A(d) gives both credits the SAME threshold and the SAME range, so a return whose AOTC is phased out to zero has a Lifetime Learning Credit phased out to zero too.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT REACH, disclosed rather than assumed: a return with two or more students where the SAME student's expenses appear in both boxes is not distinguishable from a return where they do not, other than through the attestation — this module has one Part III, one student name and one student TIN. The per-student Part III collection is the shape that would derive the answer instead of asking for it; see /writableLlcExpensesIncludeAotcStudent.

Fact.Name: Student did not receive a 2025 Form 1098-T from the second institution (Form 8863 line 22b)
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 8863 Part III line 22b(2). A checkbox mapping names one Bool and the filler sets the box when that Bool is true, so the No box needs a fact of its own: this is Not(/writableForm8863SecondInstitutionCurrentYear1098T). Incompleteness propagates through Not, so an unanswered question leaves the No box blank as well as the Yes box, and the pair can never both print. The line 22a twin is /form8863FirstInstitutionNoCurrentYear1098T.

Fact.Name: Student did not receive a 2024 Form 1098-T with box 7 checked from the second institution (Form 8863 line 22b)
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 8863 Part III line 22b(3): Not(/writableForm8863SecondInstitutionPriorYear1098TBox7).
