Same shape and same reasoning as the line 22b(2) pair: a checkbox mapping names one Bool, so the No box needs its own fact, and incompleteness propagates through Not so an unanswered question prints neither box. The line 22a twin is /form8863FirstInstitutionNoPriorYear1098TBox7.

Fact.Name: Zero dollar floor for the Form 8863 Part III lines (structural)
Fact.Description: A $0 Dollar fact, the floor Form 8863 Part III line 28 names when it says "If zero or less, enter -0-" and the comparison point line 30 names when it asks whether line 28 is zero. A greater of and a greater than both take two Dollar FACTS, so the constant needs a name; the module level zero literal is the shape dictionary/ty2025 already uses at /form5329ZeroFloorAmount, /scheduleEZeroDollarFloor and /partIILineTwelveZeroFloor. Structural rather than a param ledger amount: zero is a floor, not a statutory dollar figure that could ever be indexed.

Fact.Name: Lifetime Learning Credit qualified expense cap (Form 8863 line 11 constant)
Fact.Description: The $10,000 printed on Form 8863 Part II line 11, "Enter the smaller of line 10 or $10,000", as a fact so the line 11 smaller-of can be built from two Dollar facts. The amount is the statutory Lifetime Learning Credit expense ceiling of IRC 25A(c)(1) and already carries a param-ledger id in this repo: authority/ty2025/parameters.tsv records llc-expense-cap for 8863 line 11 at 10000, and dictionary/ty2025/form8863.xml tags its inline copy of the same constant with that id inside /llcCreditBeforePhaseout. This fact names it once instead of a second time inline.

Fact.Name: Lifetime Learning Credit qualified expenses up to the cap (Form 8863 line 11)
Fact.Description:
Form 8863 Part II line 11, the smaller of line 10 and $10,000. Line 10 is /writableLlcQualifiedExpenses, which the register already prints at f1_15[0], and line 12 is /llcCreditBeforePhaseout; line 11, the step between them, had no fact because dictionary/ty2025/form8863.xml folds LesserOf(expenses, 10000) into that line 12 Multiply by one fifth and never names the intermediate. This fact names it, and the arithmetic is identical to the arithmetic already inside line 12, so the printed column foots.
TWO DIFFERENCES FROM LINE 12 ARE DELIBERATE AND DISCLOSED. First, this fact carries no married-filing-separately gate: an MFS filer is ineligible for the credit and line 12 resolves 0 for one, but line 11 as printed is only "the smaller of line 10 or $10,000", and the shipped register already prints line 10 unguarded, so gating line 11 would make the printed page inconsistent with itself rather than more correct. Second, it is not complete-safe by design: with line 10 unanswered the smaller-of is unanswered too, so line 11 stays blank exactly as a filer with no Lifetime Learning expenses would leave it.

Fact.Name: Form 8862 Line 18a student name box
Fact.Description: What the PDF box prints. Form 8862 line 18a is printed only when Form 8862 is the American Opportunity Credit recertification, so the student name is printed when /aotc8862Required is true and the box is left empty otherwise. Without the gate the name would print on an EIC only or CTC only Form 8862, which renders Part IV blank.

Fact.Name: Form 8862 Line 19a No checkbox
Fact.Description: Whether the PDF checkbox should be checked. The No box of the line 19a pair: checked when Form 8862 is required for the AOTC and the student did not meet the eligible student requirements, which is the answer the printed Caution says bars the credit for that student.

Fact.Name: Form 8862 Line 19a Yes checkbox
Fact.Description: Whether the PDF checkbox should be checked. Form 8862 line 19a is printed only when Form 8862 is the American Opportunity Credit recertification, so the box is checked when Form 8862 is required for the AOTC and the taxpayer says the student met the eligible student requirements.

Fact.Name: Form 8862 Line 19b No checkbox
Fact.Description: Whether the PDF checkbox should be checked. The No box of the line 19b pair: checked when Form 8862 is required for the AOTC and the credit has not already been claimed for this student for 4 prior tax years.

Fact.Name: Form 8862 Line 19b Yes checkbox
Fact.Description: Whether the PDF checkbox should be checked. Checked when Form 8862 is required for the AOTC and the credit has already been claimed for this student for 4 prior tax years, the answer the printed Caution says bars the credit for that student.

Fact.Name: Hope Scholarship Credit or AOTC was claimed for the student for 4 prior tax years
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's answer to Form 8862 line 19b: whether the Hope Scholarship Credit or the American Opportunity Credit has been claimed for this student for any 4 tax years before the year entered on line 1. A writable because the graph keeps no prior year credit history for a student. When Form 8862 is required, /aotcStudentEligibleForAotc reads this answer and a Yes stops the credit.

Fact.Name: American Opportunity Credit was claimed for this student for any 4 prior tax years (Form 8863 line 23)
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's answer to Form 8863 Part III line 23: whether the American Opportunity Credit has been claimed for THIS student for any 4 prior tax years. A writable because the graph keeps no prior year credit history for a student. YES is the barring answer (Stop, go to line 31), so the Yes box is this writable and the No box, which continues to line 24, is /aotcStudentNotClaimedForFourPriorTaxYears. /aotcStudentEligibleForAotc reads this answer and /aotcTentativeCredit reads that gate, so the printed Stop instruction stops the credit.
WHY THIS IS NOT THE STAGED FORM 8862 FACT. /writableAotcClaimedForFourPriorTaxYears sits in this same module for Form 8862 line 19b, and the two questions restate one statutory test, the 4 taxable year election bar of IRC 25A(b)(2)(A). They are nevertheless kept apart, for two reasons written down rather than assumed. First, the year anchors differ: Form 8862 line 19b counts the 4 prior years against the year entered on its own line 1, which is the year being recertified and need not be 2025, while Form 8863 line 23 counts them against this return's tax year. Second, the Form 8862 side is reshaped per student, into a /form8862AotcStudents collection, whose per item leaves Form 8863 could not print anyway without a dictionary/pdf/2025/column-axes.tsv row for IRS8863. Sharing one fact across that boundary would wire a printed Form 8863 line to a fact whose scope is moving. This fact is the Form 8863 Part III gate, return level at the module's declared single student scope and carrying the credit rewire obligation the Form 8862 attestation does not.

Fact.Name: Student completed the first 4 years of postsecondary education before 2025 (Form 8863 line 25)
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's answer to Form 8863 Part III line 25: whether the student completed the first 4 years of postsecondary education before 2025. A writable for the same reason as line 24: the graph carries no education history for a student. Note the printed polarity is inverted against line 24: here YES is the barring answer (Stop, go to line 31) and NO continues to line 26, so the Yes box is this writable itself and the No box is /aotcStudentDidNotCompleteFirstFourYears. /aotcStudentEligibleForAotc reads this answer and /aotcTentativeCredit reads that gate, so the printed Stop instruction stops the credit.

Fact.Name: Student was enrolled at least half time for at least one 2025 academic period (Form 8863 line 24)
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's answer to Form 8863 Part III line 24: whether the student was enrolled at least half time for at least one academic period that began or is treated as having begun in 2025 at an eligible educational institution in a program leading toward a postsecondary degree, certificate, or other recognized postsecondary educational credential. A writable because dictionary/ty2025/form8863.xml states in its own scope note that the Part III student eligibility gates are DEFERRED: nothing in the graph records enrollment status, academic periods or degree programs, so there is nothing to derive this from and the form asks the taxpayer directly. TRUE fills the Yes box (go to line 25); the No box (Stop, go to line 31) is /aotcStudentNotEnrolledAtLeastHalfTime. Unanswered leaves both blank. /aotcStudentEligibleForAotc reads this answer and /aotcTentativeCredit reads that gate, so the printed Stop instruction stops the credit.

Fact.Name: Student was convicted of a felony drug offense before the end of 2025 (Form 8863 line 26)
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's answer to Form 8863 Part III line 26: whether the student was convicted, before the end of 2025, of a felony for possession or distribution of a controlled substance. A writable because the graph holds no criminal history of any kind. YES is the barring answer (Stop, go to line 31), so the Yes box is this writable and the No box, which continues to lines 27 through 30, is /aotcStudentNoFelonyDrugConviction. /aotcStudentEligibleForAotc reads this answer and /aotcTentativeCredit reads that gate, so the printed Stop instruction stops the credit.

Fact.Name: Student met the eligible student requirements for the AOTC
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's answer to Form 8862 line 19a: whether the student met the requirements to be an eligible student for purposes of the American Opportunity Credit for the year entered on line 1. A writable: Form 8862 asks the taxpayer directly. The Form 8863 Part III tests that decide the credit are /aotcStudentEligibleForAotc; this answer is printed and is not reconciled with them.

Fact.Name: Name of the student on Form 8862 Part IV
Fact.Description: The name of the student for whom the American Opportunity Credit is claimed, as listed on Form 8863, supplied directly by the taxpayer. Form 8862 line 18a asks for it. The graph carries no student identity of its own: form8863.xml scopes the credit to one student and never names them, and Form 8863's own student name box prints the filer names, so this is an intake, not a derivation. Print only for Student 1 until the graph grows an AOTC student collection; students 2 and 3 have no source.

Fact.Name: Address of the first educational institution (Form 8863 line 22a)
Fact.Description: Form 8863 Part III line 22a(1), the first educational institution's number and street or P.O. box, city, town or post office, state and ZIP code, supplied directly by the taxpayer. The template prints it into one free-text box, so one String intake fills it; the graph has no institution address anywhere to derive it from. Return-level, single student and first institution scope, matching /writableAotcQualifiedExpenses. Print only: no computation consumes it.

Fact.Name: Student received a 2025 Form 1098-T from the first institution (Form 8863 line 22a)
Fact.Description: Screen question: Form 8863 Part III line 22a(2), "Did the student receive Form 1098-T from this institution for 2025?". An ATTESTATION, not a computation: a Form 1098-T is a payee statement the institution furnishes under section 6050S, and this dictionary carries no 1098-T document, so whether one arrived cannot be derived from the return. TRUE fills the Yes box; the No box is /form8863FirstInstitutionNoCurrentYear1098T, the negation of this fact. Unanswered leaves BOTH boxes blank, which is the honest rendering of a question nobody has asked yet. Return-level, single student and first institution scope. Help text: answering No surfaces a follow-up asking whether the 1098-T exception applies (/writableForm8863First1098TExceptionApplies). CONDITION OF ALLOWANCE (IRC 25A(g)(8)): feeds /aotcFirstInstitutionPayeeStatementMet → /aotcIdentificationAndPayeeStatementMet, which gates /aotcTentativeCredit, and /llcPayeeStatementMet, which gates /llcCreditBeforePhaseout — this is no longer print-only. Unanswered posture: on a return that claims the AOTC for this student, leaves the credit Incomplete (disclosed as unfinished, not a silent $0); on a return that never claims the AOTC, this question is moot. An ANSWERED No with no exception attested still bars the credit deterministically (see /aotcFirstInstitutionPayeeStatementMet). Validation: Boolean.

Fact.Name: First educational institution EIN (Form 8863 line 22a(4))
Fact.Description: The employer identification number of the first eligible educational institution on Form 8863 line 22a(4), an intake from Form 1098-T. Printed through nine single-digit boxes by the ~einDigit1..9 filler transforms declared in transforms.tsv. Asked-when: whenever AOTC expenses are entered. CONDITION OF ALLOWANCE (IRC 25A(g)(1)(B)(iii), AOTC-only): feeds /aotcIdentificationAndPayeeStatementMet, which gates /aotcTentativeCredit. Unanswered posture: on a return that claims the AOTC for this student, leaves the credit Incomplete (disclosed as unfinished, not a silent $0); on a return that never claims the AOTC, this question is moot. Validation: EIN.

Fact.Name: Name of the first educational institution (Form 8863 line 22a)
Fact.Description:
Form 8863 Part III line 22a, "Name of first educational institution", supplied directly by the taxpayer. Nothing in this dictionary carries educational-institution information: the module's scope note defers the Part III student and institution detail, and there is no 1098-T document collection to read a payer name from.
SCOPE, STATED PLAINLY: this is a return-level writable at the module's declared single student, first institution scope, the same scope at which Part III line 27 is already the return-level /writableAotcQualifiedExpenses. It is PRINT ONLY: no computation consumes it, because IRC 25A(g)(1)(B)(iii) makes the institution identification a condition of allowance rather than a term of the credit arithmetic. Fact.Name: Form 8863 line 6 in thousandths, as the division and rounding nodes first produce it
Fact.Description: 1000 times line 4 (floored at zero) divided by line 5, rounded to a whole number of thousandths and capped at 1000, when line 5 is above $0; $0 otherwise. This is an intermediate figure and not the printed line. A Dollar division is reduced to cents (half to even) before the outer Round takes it to whole thousandths (half up), so a true quotient a fraction of a cent below one half of a thousandth is rounded up; the cent reduction moves a value by at most half a cent, so the only possible error here is one thousandth too high. /aotcPhaseoutFractionThousandths corrects that step with exact cent arithmetic.

Fact.Name: American Opportunity Credit phaseout fraction times 1000 (Form 8863 line 6)
Fact.Description: Form 8863 Part I line 6 = line 4 divided by line 5, entered as a decimal rounded to at least three places and capped at 1.000, represented here as INTEGER THOUSANDTHS so it can be an exact Dollar value: line 6 times 1000. The numerator is /educationCreditPhaseoutHeadroomFloored (the printed line 4 clamped at zero, because line 4 says to stop when it is zero or less) and the denominator is /aotcPhaseoutRange (the printed line 5). MULTIPLY FIRST, DIVIDE LAST: scaling by 1000 before the divide keeps the third decimal place, which a Dollar quotient taken at two places would already have lost. The 1.000 ceiling the printed line states for the equal to or more than branch is the LesserOf against 1000. Complete safe 0 when the range is not positive. CANONICAL FOR THE CREDIT TOO: /aotcCreditAfterPhaseout multiplies /aotcTentativeCredit by THIS fact and divides by 1,000 afterwards, which is what "Multiply line 1 by line 6" asks for and what makes the printed line 6 and the printed line 7 foot. One quantity, one fact: this is the only phaseout ratio in the module. It is the encoding /adoptionPhaseoutFractionThousandths already uses for Form 8839 line 9, and the two printed boxes read it through the integerPart and thousandthsPart filler transforms. The printed decimal is ONE half-up rounding of the true quotient: this fact starts from /aotcPhaseoutFractionRoundedAfterCentSnap and steps it down by one thousandth exactly when 2,000 times line 4 is less than (2 times that figure minus 1) times line 5, the exact cent comparison saying the true quotient is below the lower half-thousandth boundary. Every product in that comparison is a whole number of cents, so no rounding enters the test.

Fact.Name: Education credit MAGI headroom, floored at zero (Form 8863 lines 4 and 15, the clamp the ratio divides)
Fact.Description: The greater of /educationCreditPhaseoutMagiHeadroom and /form8863ZeroFloorAmount: the phaseout threshold minus modified adjusted gross income, never below zero. The printed lines 4 and 15 carry the RAW subtraction and may be negative, which is why /educationCreditPhaseoutMagiHeadroom is unfloored and stays that way; this fact is the clamped numerator the line 6 and line 17 ratios divide, and it is the ONLY clamp in the module: /aotcCreditAfterPhaseout and /llcCreditAfterPhaseout read the two ratio facts this one feeds rather than nesting an unnamed copy of the same GreaterOf. Lines 4 and 15 both say to stop or to skip ahead when the difference is zero or less, so a nonpositive headroom produces a zero fraction rather than a negative one; the floor is the printed instruction, not an invention. NOT PRINTED ITSELF: nothing on Form 8863 shows this value, it exists so the two ratio facts below have a Dollar numerator that cannot go negative.

Fact.Name: Lifetime Learning Credit phaseout fraction times 1000 (Form 8863 line 17)
Fact.Description: Form 8863 Part II line 17 = line 15 divided by line 16, entered as a decimal rounded to at least three places and capped at 1.000, carried as INTEGER THOUSANDTHS exactly as /aotcPhaseoutFractionThousandths carries line 6. The numerator is /educationCreditPhaseoutHeadroomFloored (the printed line 15 clamped at zero) and the denominator is /aotcPhaseoutRange (the printed line 16). ARITHMETICALLY IDENTICAL TO LINE 6 TODAY AND DELIBERATELY A SEPARATE FACT: this module already serves lines 4 and 15 from one headroom fact and prints /aotcPhaseoutThreshold on lines 2 and 13 and /aotcPhaseoutRange on lines 5 and 16, because current law gives the two credits the same threshold and the same range. The two printed lines are still two lines of two different Parts governed by IRC 25A(d) separately, and /llcCreditAfterPhaseout already keeps its own copy of the arithmetic for the same reason. Collapsing line 6 and line 17 onto one fact is a naming decision for the module owner, not something this printed line can assume. Complete safe 0 when the range is not positive; /llcCreditAfterPhaseout multiplies line 12 by THIS fact and divides by 1,000 afterwards, so the printed ratio is the only one it uses. ONE QUANTITY, ONE FACT (operator rule): this fact is a direct alias of /aotcPhaseoutFractionThousandths (IRC 25A(d) sets one MAGI phaseout range for both education credits in TY2025, so line 17 equals line 6 on every return: the same floored headroom over the same range), which computes the identical quantity.
